audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 gave the stage to Sion (or Skill) while whys[1], whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5] each say Sett is ahead there, and mid says 'levels 3-6 belong to Sett'.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is a 10s telegraphed charge that only stuns at full wind-up; Sett out-trades him in every gap until Sion's tank items land.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 5 -> Sett with ratings raised. Row 6 stays Sion — that is where his scaling actually lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text claimed Soul Furnace 'grants a burst of AD when it expires', repeated in wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Riot's text: Sion shields himself and can REACTIVATE after 3 seconds to deal magic damage; the only passive gain is maximum Health on kills. There is no AD component.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the 15s cooldown and the 3-second reactivation.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named a single Sion ability outside the templated 'Decimating Smash (Stun)', and it asserted Sett's R applies a suppression Sion cannot cancel.
audit.why: Only a FULLY charged Decimating Smash knocks up and stuns — a partial release just damages, which is the whole trading rhythm. Roar of the Slayer additionally shreds your armour at 800 range and knocks a minion back through you. Sett's R is described only as a carry-and-slam; suppression behaviour is not in this data, so the interrupt claim is not assertable.
audit.corrected: Real names and cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t; the suppression claim removed from spikes[1].text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (Q cd 10/9/8/7/6, E cd 12/11/10/9/8 range 800, R cd 140/100/60)

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstoppable Onslaught creates terrain and Sett has no dash — it cuts the retreat.
audit.why: Flagged in _kits/_missing as terrain-cuts-retreat; nothing on the page mentioned it.
Executioner's Calling is already the first back, which is the right answer to Glory in Death's on-hit healing.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash (Stun): matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. Track it before every engage. - Sion Decimating Smash: Charged swing; fully charged it knocks up in a big area. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash: 10s at rank 1 — only a full charge knocks up and stuns, so step out during the wind-up. - Sion Roar of the Slayer: 12s at rank 1, shreds your armour and knocks a minion back through you.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 10s at rank 1, and only a full charge stuns. Trade in the wind-up.

edits.before: Track Sion's Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. When it is down — E-stun + W him.
edits.after: Only a fully charged Decimating Smash knocks up — walk out of the wind-up, then E-stun into the W panel.

edits.before: That is Sion's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: You have no dash — he cuts your retreat with R, so hold Flash for the wall, not damage.

edits.before: Your Show Stopper beats his ultimate charge: R him mid-Unstoppable-Onslaught to stop the knock-up, since he can't cancel your suppression once it lands.
edits.after: The Show Stopper flips him at 6 while Unstoppable Onslaught sits on 140s at rank 1 — fight in the gap after he burns the charge, never while it is up.

edits.before: After a bruiser item you win every non-Q trade; just respect his shield W, which grants a burst of AD when it expires.
edits.after: After a bruiser item you win every non-Q trade; respect Soul Furnace, a 15s shield he reactivates after 3s for magic damage.

edits.before: Pop W shield before a trade so it expires into bonus AD damage
edits.after: Pop Soul Furnace, then reactivate it after 3s for the burst

edits.before: Show Stopper cleanly interrupts his level 6 ult or charged Q.
edits.after: The Show Stopper at 6 beats his 140s Unstoppable Onslaught.

notes: Mirror not yet audited. Two claims removed rather than repeated: Soul Furnace granting bonus AD on expiry (not in Riot's text at all) and The Show Stopper applying a suppression that beats Unstoppable Onslaught (the kit calls it a carry-and-slam; suppression, and whether R can catch a champion mid-charge, is outside this data). Both recorded in unverified.
